clauses.current_legal_basis: Continuing: the held U.S. Code note under 3 U.S.C. 301 (release point 119-121, through 2026-10-09) prints EO 10621 as amended by EO 12561 with subsection (h), and 5 U.S.C. 5702(a)(1) (held text) still vests in the President or his designee the power to establish per diem and expense limits for travel outside the continental United States; no later held instrument amends subsection (h).
clauses.reason: Operative on 2026-10-14. The amendment instruction was carried out on signing: current subsection (i) of section 1 of EO 10621 was redesignated (g), subsection (o) was revoked and a new subsection (h) added. The held 3 U.S.C. 301 note prints subsection (h) in the current text of EO 10621, with the same words and the amendment list ending at EO 12561, so the amended text of EO 10621 stands.

clauses.current_legal_basis: Continuing: 5 U.S.C. 5702(a)(1)(A)-(B) (held current text) refers to limits established by the President or his designee for travel outside the continental United States; the held U.S. Code note under 5 U.S.C. 5702 (release point 119-121) prints section 2 with no ending.
clauses.reason: Operative on 2026-10-14. Section 2 delegates to the Secretary of State the President's authority under 5 U.S.C. 5702(a) to set maximum per diem and actual-expense limits for travel in areas outside the United States. The statute now reads that the limits for travel outside the continental United States are those set by the President or his designee, and the held 5 U.S.C. 5702 note prints this section as current text.

clauses.current_legal_basis: Continuing effect: EO 11294 is not among the orders held as in force, the held 3 U.S.C. 301 note lists it only as an earlier amendment of EO 10621, and the held 5 U.S.C. 5702 note prints section 3; the bounded searches name no instrument reviving or ending this revocation.
clauses.reason: Operative as a completed revocation whose effect stands. Section 3 revoked EO 11294 of August 4, 1966 (the earlier delegation of the per diem authority, replaced by sections 1 and 2 here); the revocation took effect on signing and no held instrument revives EO 11294. The held U.S. Code note still prints section 3 as part of the order.

research_rationale:
Identity: the held Federal Register original (51 FR 24299, PDF page 13) is Executive Order 12561 of July 1, 1986, Ronald Reagan, Delegating Certain Functions of the President Relating to Federal Civilian Employee and Contractor Travel Expenses. Three sections: section 1 amends section 1 of Executive Order 10621 (redesignating subsection (i) as (g), revoking (o), adding subsection (h) on the President's authority under 5 U.S.C. 5702(a) for Alaska, Hawaii, Puerto Rico and possessions); section 2 delegates the same authority for areas outside the United States to the Secretary of State; section 3 revokes Executive Order 11294. Current law: the held text of 5 U.S.C. 5702(a)(1)(A)-(B) still gives the President or his designee the power to set per diem and actual-expense limits for travel outside the continental United States; the held U.S. Code note under 3 U.S.C. 301 prints EO 10621 as amended through EO 12561 with subsection (h) in the current text, and the note under 5 U.S.C. 5702 prints this order, both through release point 119-121 (2026-10-09), with no ending. No later amendment or revocation is held.
